{"path":"snake_openrouter-moonshotai-kimi-k3_01.html","edit_description":"Create a NEW complete single-file HTML game (embedded CSS in <style> and JS in <script>, no external dependencies) implementing a two-snake competitive Snake game on a 30x30 grid. The file must be fully self-contained and work when opened directly in a browser.

REQUIREMENTS:

1. GRID & RENDERING
- 30x30 logical grid rendered on a <canvas> (e.g. 600x600 px, 20px cells), dark background with subtle grid lines.
- Snakes drawn as filled rounded-ish rectangles with a slightly brighter head; food drawn as a red circle/apple.

2. GAME ENTITIES
- Two snakes always on the board: Snake 1 (green, starts left side moving right) and Snake 2 (orange/amber, starts right side moving left). Each has: body array of {x,y} cells (head first), current direction, queued next direction, score, alive flag.
- One food item at a time, spawned on a random cell not occupied by either snake.

3. MOVEMENT & RULES
- Fixed-timestep game loop (e.g. tick every 100ms via setInterval or rAF accumulator). Snakes move continuously one cell per tick in their current direction.
- Direction reversal 180° is forbidden (queue input and validate against the direction that will be current at next tick).
- Eating food: snake grows by 1 (tail not removed that tick), score +1, new food spawns.
- Death conditions per snake: hitting a wall (leaving the 30x30 grid), hitting its own body, hitting the other snake's body. Head-on-head collision in the same tick: both die.
- When a snake dies the game ends immediately. Winner = surviving snake; if both die the same tick, higher score wins (tie allowed). Show which snake won and why (e.g. "Snake 1 hit the wall").

4. CPU AI (for cpu-controlled snakes)
- Each tick, compute the next move with BFS shortest path from the snake's head to the food over free cells (free = inside grid, not occupied by any snake body, excluding tails that will move this tick is optional — simple version: treat all snake body cells as blocked).
- If BFS finds a path, take the first step of it. If no path exists, pick any non-lethal neighboring move (prefer the move that keeps the most free space, e.g. count reachable cells via flood fill and pick the max). If no safe move exists, keep going straight.
- AI must never reverse direction.

5. GAME MODES (selected from start menu)
- "Human vs Human": Snake 1 controlled by WASD, Snake 2 by Arrow keys.
- "CPU vs Human": Snake 1 human-controlled (Arrow keys AND WASD both work), Snake 2 is CPU.
- "CPU vs CPU": both snakes AI-controlled (spectator mode).
Store mode in a variable; startGame(mode) resets everything.

6. UI SCREENS (HTML overlays over the canvas, toggled with a .hidden class)
- START MENU: game title "SNAKE", three buttons (also selectable with keys 1/2/3): "1 - Human vs Human", "2 - CPU vs Human", "3 - CPU vs CPU", plus a controls legend (WASD / Arrows, R to restart, M for menu).
- HUD during gameplay: always-visible score bar above the canvas showing "P1: <score>" and "P2: <score>" (label them CPU when AI-controlled, e.g. "CPU 1", "CPU 2"), updated live every food eaten.
- GAME OVER screen: "GAME OVER", winner announcement with scores (e.g. "Snake 1 wins! 7 - 3" or "Draw!"), the death reason, and "Press R to play again - Press M for menu".

7. KEYBOARD CONTROLS
- keydown listener: WASD + Arrow keys steer the human snake(s); preventDefault on arrows/space so the page doesn't scroll. Keys 1/2/3 select mode from the menu. R restarts the current mode instantly from the game-over screen (and during gameplay too). M returns to the start menu. Ignore input when snake is CPU or game is not running.

8. STYLE
- Dark neon arcade look: near-black page background, centered layout, glowing green title, monospace/arcade font stack, buttons with hover effect. All CSS in <style> in <head>.

Make sure the JS is complete, bug-free, and self-initializing (show start menu on load). No external libraries, no images, no network calls."}
